title: Certificate-Based VPN Authentication for Cisco ISE with Intune (SCEP/PKCS)
hook: Replace VPN passwords with certificates Cisco ISE trusts
problem: Password-based VPN is the weak link Cisco ISE was built to remove — but issuing the right device or user certificate to every endpoint, with a trust chain ISE validates, defeats most teams. This solution stands up certificate-based VPN authentication end to end: issue certs from Intune via SCEP (Certificate Connector / NDES or Cloud PKI) or PKCS, deploy the trusted-root and certificate profiles, and hand Cisco ISE a clean EAP-TLS identity to authenticate — deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — how EAP-TLS certificate VPN auth works with ISE as the RADIUS authority, the SCEP vs PKCS choice, the trust chain ISE must validate, and where Intune's cert delivery meets the Cisco head-end.

Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (a CA / Cloud PKI, the Intune Certificate Connector or NDES/SCEP, trusted-root + SCEP/PKCS profiles, Entra ID groups, ISE configured for EAP-TLS) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.

Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps to build the trusted-root profile, the SCEP or PKCS certificate profile, assign to a named pilot group, confirm certs land, and validate ISE accepts the EAP-TLS handshake, then pilot and expand.

5 PowerShell scripts — certificate-readiness discovery, per-device certificate + chain validation, a certificate deployment/expiry coverage report, safe remediation of missing/failed certs, and a target-group builder.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates (cert present, chain valid, ISE auth success), plus field-proven Best Practices for renewal and revocation.
short: Issue device/user certificates from Intune (SCEP or PKCS) with a trust chain Cisco ISE validates — passwordless EAP-TLS VPN authentication, deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
